question.stem: An extraction agent completes its turn, but the receiving worker rejects this handoff. Which change best repairs the boundary while preserving source fidelity and limiting repeated model calls?

options.text: Validate against the consumer contract; return exact field errors with the source; allow bounded repair and route unresolved defects to review.
options.why: The receiver owns acceptance and can request supported corrections without inventing missing evidence.

options.text: Enable supported schema-constrained generation and accept the next conforming record without source checks.
options.why: Constrained generation improves shape but does not prove units or agreement with the invoice.

options.text: Coerce numeric values to integers and populate absent required strings with a standard placeholder before validation.
options.why: Coercion can silently change money, and a placeholder invents a PO rather than representing absence.

options.text: Force the extraction tool with tool_choice and retry the unchanged prompt until the worker accepts it.
options.why: Selection does not correct the contract defect, and unbounded identical retries do not resolve its cause.

question.translation: Can the next program use these fields, and how can we fix them without making facts up?

repair.narration: Add the receiving validator. It rejects fractional cents and the missing key. Correct from the source: 8450 cents and an explicit null PO. Acceptance follows checks; completing a model turn does not accept the invoice.

question.stem: Which recovery design best isolates heterogeneous failures without discarding completed work or overstating archive completeness?

options.text: Track API status only; regenerate any missing downstream record from its last model response.
options.why: API status does not identify unreadable preparation or prove downstream acceptance.

options.text: Persist stable source/version IDs with separate preparation, API, validation and downstream states; recover only eligible failures by cause.
options.why: This preserves A, routes B to preparation/review and permits bounded C retry with correct identity.

options.text: Create one new batch for all source files and replace the archive when its processing status is terminal.
options.why: Terminal state does not establish every item succeeded, and reprocessing accepted work adds duplication risk.

options.text: Retry every failed ID with exponential backoff, including unreadable input, until the archive deadline.
options.why: Backoff addresses transient conditions, not missing or unusable source evidence.

question.translation: Which file worked, which needs a different remedy, and what is still unfinished?

stages.title: The agreement changes
stages.kicker: Transfer: omission is now allowed

question.stem: How should the producer adopt v2 without confusing absent evidence with extraction failure or breaking the remaining consumer?

options.text: Remove purchase_order from every output and migrate consumers implicitly through the next successful request.
options.why: The v1 consumer still requires the field and has not agreed to an implicit migration.

options.text: Keep the v1 schema but normalize every null into an empty string before delivery to both consumers.
options.why: An empty string changes the agreed meaning rather than implementing versioned presence rules.

options.text: Version the producer-consumer agreement, validate against the intended consumer version, and preserve explicit absence/failure meanings.
options.why: Presence rules can change by contract while source fidelity and consumer compatibility stay explicit.

options.text: Make every output include a generated PO reference so both versions retain a stable field.
options.why: Compatibility does not justify generating evidence absent from the invoice.

question.translation: Did the source change, or only the agreement between programs?

courseConnections.title: Claude Platform 101
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: The backend must obtain actual evidence and pass it to the model; a resource address is not document text. For a client-tool variant, define a read-only lookup tool, handle the proposed call in backend code, return the observed result correlated to that call, then request the explanation. Keep MCP resource reading distinct from this alternative. More thinking cannot fetch an unread manual. Built-in web tools do not replace the approved private manual store; reusable skills package procedures, not access rights. A managed runtime becomes a candidate only if session/lifecycle needs justify it.

courseConnections.title: Claude Code 101
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Implement the maintenance service with a narrow, testable code change. Use Claude Code to inspect the repository and relevant caller contracts, plan a scoped change, implement it, and run targeted negative and happy-path tests; review the diff and executed evidence. Put the retrieval invariant and test commands in CLAUDE.md as guidance; use deterministic tests or approved hooks for checks. Package a repeatable review as a skill when useful, and commit only after reviewing actual results.

courseConnections.title: Introduction to Model Context Protocol
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Discovering an MCP resource and reading its content are separate events. Trace catalog discovery, selected resource read and context assembly. In the current fixture, the read fails; preserve that status and report unavailable evidence. A resource exposes addressable content; a tool performs a callable search/read operation; an MCP prompt is a reusable interaction template. None grants the technician new entitlement, and host support determines what is available.

courseConnections.title: Introduction to subagents
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Decide whether a specialist improves this single-manual question. Start without subagents. Only evaluate a specialist if a changed requirement needs separate bounded investigation, such as an independent source-authority audit, and keep final synthesis ownership explicit.

courseConnections.title: Product Foundations
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Choose the product surface for the actual user and workflow. Use the embedded backend service for a governed technician workflow; a human-reviewed exploration interface may aid learning, while developer tooling implements the service. Do not assume changing the surface transfers application authorization to the model.

courseConnections.title: Deployment Architecture
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Place the application, evidence store, model endpoint and controls within an approved deployment boundary. Document who processes what data and where. If a gateway/proxy is required, define authentication, scoped routing, redaction/logging and failure behavior; it must not bypass source authorization or silently route sensitive evidence to an unapproved endpoint. Compare the direct Claude API with the organization’s approved cloud route, such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud or Microsoft Foundry; verify the actual endpoint instead of assuming feature or data-handling parity.

courseConnections.title: Delivery Methodology
courseConnections.connection: Applied to this case: Deliver a pilot that improves evidence-backed maintenance answers without disguising unresolved risk. Record baseline errors/time, define success and failure cases with the maintenance owner, test representative users, review access and escalation risks, then decide whether to expand. Keep operational approval outside the answer demo.
